info.title: Portitor identity
info.description: The public HTTP interface of portitor-identity (ADR 0015): the participant's did:web DID document, the Secure Token Service for its own connector, the DCP v1.0.1 credential service (presentation, storage and offer APIs), and the certificate chain and Gaia-X credentials of ADR 0021. Message bodies follow the DCP v1.0.1 JSON Schemas (copies in crates/portitor-dcp/tests/schemas, linked from each operation). The management API is described separately in identity-management-openapi.json. Written by hand; a test checks that every operation here is served.

servers.description: The identity's public address (PORTITOR_BIND behind HTTPS)

get.description: Served at the path the did:web method gives for PORTITOR_PARTICIPANT_ID: /.well-known/did.json for a DID without a path, /<path>/did.json otherwise. One P-256 verification method for the current key (authentication, assertionMethod, capabilityInvocation), whose publicKeyJwk has alg ES256 (RFC 7517 section 4.4) and, when PORTITOR_IDENTITY_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN is set, x5u: the URL of /.well-known/x509CertificateChain.pem, below the DID path for a DID with one (RFC 7517 section 4.6, ADR 0021); after it, one for each retired public key in PORTITOR_IDENTITY_RETIRED_KEY_FILES, with the same relationships and alg, never x5u (TD-05); each id is <did>#<JWK thumbprint>; and the CredentialService entry.

post.summary: A self-issued ID token for the participant's own connector (STS)
post.description: DCP's non-normative STS interface (identity-trust-sts-api.yaml, tag v1.0.1). Only the configured client (PORTITOR_STS_CLIENT_ID and its secret) gets tokens.

audience.description: The DID the token is for (its aud)

bearer_access_scope.description: Space-separated scopes: the token gets a token claim that lets audience read those credentials

token.description: Another participant's access token, passed on in the token claim (when this participant verifies)

400.description: The request is not a valid token request

post.description: The caller sends a self-issued ID token as Authorization: Bearer; its token claim must be an access token this identity's STS signed for that caller. Queries by scope only; presentation definitions are not supported.

200.description: PresentationResponseMessage, one presentation per credential profile

401.description: The caller or its access token was refused

501.description: The query uses a presentation definition

post.summary: Storage API: an issuer delivers credentials (DCP 6.5)
post.description: Accepted only for a credential request the participant made (management API), from the issuer it was made to.

400.description: Not a valid delivery, or not one the participant asked for

post.summary: Credential Offer API: an issuer says credentials are available (DCP 6.6)
post.description: Offers are recorded and listed in the management API; nothing is requested automatically.

get.summary: The X.509 certificate chain of the participant's key
get.description: The file PORTITOR_IDENTITY_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN, PEM: the certificate for the key in the DID document first, then its chain. The DID document's JWK points here with x5u (RFC 7517 section 4.6), as Gaia-X needs (ADR 0021). For a DID with a path (did:web:host:participants:a) the route is below that path: /participants/a/.well-known/x509CertificateChain.pem. A renewed file for the same key is served without a restart. 404 when no chain is set.

get.summary: A Gaia-X credential of the participant, as VC-JWT
get.description: The credentials the last good Gaia-X compliance run sent (ADR 0021), at their ids, so anyone can recompute their digests; for a DID with a path the route is below that path (/participants/a/credentials/gaiax/{name}): legal-person (gx:LegalPerson) and terms-and-conditions (gx:Issuer), signed by the participant's key, and registration-number, the registration number credential a GXDCH notary issued. The compliance credential itself is not served here; verifiers get it through the presentation API.

404.description: No such credential, or no good compliance run yet

selfIssuedIdToken.description: A self-issued ID token (DCP base protocol, section 4.3), checked against the caller's DID document
